title: Editing orchestrator source: commit atomically — git is the only durable anchor
summary: Confirmed this session: the self-learning AUTO_MERGE loop rewrites the orchestrator working tree (daemon.js) roughly every 1-2 min AND reuses/overwrites shared /tmp scratch paths (/tmp/daemon.js, /tmp/daemon-work.js, etc.). An uncommitted /tmp+cp edit is NOT safe — the build agent's self-heal change was wiped from BOTH the working tree and its /tmp reference within minutes because it was never committed. Mitigation that worked: (1) reconstruct/graft using a UNIQUELY-named scratch the loop won't reuse (e.g. /tmp/sh_graft_$$.js, not daemon*.js); (2) run graft→node --check→cp-to-source→test→git commit as ONE atomic bash chain (seconds, under the rewrite interval); (3) the git commit is the ONLY durable anchor — once HEAD has it, a worktree reset can't lose it; recover with git checkout HEAD -- daemon.js. Also: anchor edits on stable strings (e.g. inject before module.exports closing `};` via regex) since the loop keeps appending exports. Restart path: daemon is PPID-1 detached, no launchd/supervisor; kill it and any mcp-graph tool call respawns it via ensureDaemon() (pings 8787, spawns detached if down). Extends [[note-mq7gxx5d5h0]].
